in addition to the GitHub review itself. Format source: .claude-students/COURSE-WORKFLOW.md.
Pull the branch and test it when you can; mark each note as (required) or (optional).
Say what you checked: each AC, the cases and error paths, the test evidence, design concerns.
Notes explain each score in one or two sentences. A re-approval says what you re-checked.
If AI drafted the review, edit it, check its claims and remove this template text before posting.
Respond within 24 hours. Approve only the latest commit; review again if the author pushes after you approve.
Every student reviews at least one PR per sprint, and every teammate at least once per semester.

### Code Review — @reviewer-username

**Checked:** <what you ran or tried, which tests you ran locally, and what you checked: each AC, the cases and error paths, the test evidence, design concerns>

| Criterion | Score (1–10) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Correctness: does the change do what the issue asked? | | |
| Test coverage: are tests present and meaningful? | | |
| Test evidence: does every AC have a test? Are the expected values justified? | | |
| Code quality: consistent style, clear naming, no unnecessary duplication | | |
| Documentation: inline comments and PR description are clear | | |
| AI transparency: if AI was used, is there evidence of human verification? | | |
| Overall: would you merge this as-is? | | |
